title: Niillas Holmberg & Pauli Lyytinen: Naarattu laulu
content:
Sámi poet and musician Niillas Holmberg and Finnish saxophonist and composer Pauli Lyytinen share a complicity that seems to stem from shamanic trance. Their shared trance draws both on the ancestral mythology of the Sámi people and on the modernity of improvised music, at the far reaches of jazz and Arctic soundscapes. Together, they co-wrote the album Naarattu laulu (literally: ‘the fished out song’), which came out in 2025 on the Finnish independent label Eclipse Music. Niillas Holmberg and Pauli Lyytinen will perform together for the first time in France on 24 September 2026 at Institut finlandais.

Created around the poetic writing of Niillas Holmberg, Naarattu laulu is a deeply evocative and dreamlike work. It blends yoik (ancestral a cappella chant), spoken word, saxophone, percussion and “organic electronics” – as the performers like to call their blend of sounds captured in nature. Water flows as a recurring motif in this poetic mise en abyme tinged with surrealism; like the water of the nourishing river at the mouth of which the elders once glimpsed whales. How water carries the voice!

title: PYERI PUURRÂMLUSTO! Bon appétit !
content:
PYERI PUURRÂMLUSTO!
Bon appétit !

CHEF HEIKKI NIKULA
18 & 19 September 2026 19h00

Born and raised in Inari, in the heart of Northern Finland, Chef Heikki Nikula draws inspiration from his Inari Sámi heritage and a lifelong connection to the Arctic landscape. Growing up, he learned to fish, forage, hunt and live according to the rhythm of the northern seasons – values that continue to shape both his life and his culinary philosophy.

Inspired by his Inari Sámi heritage, Nikula’s cuisine reflects a deep respect for nature, seasonal rhythms and the ingredients of the Arctic. Each dish celebrates the pure flavours of the North and the close relationship between people and the land.

The experience will be enhanced by the radiating music of DJ Hulluella, a Sámi artist and producer based in Rovaniemi, Northern Finland. Hulluella creates immersive artistic sets that weave Indigenous Sámi joik, nature soundscapes, high-frequency textures and ambient electronics, exploring the relationship between contemporary club culture, Indigenous identity and the natural world. For this event, she will create an atmospheric Indigenous sonic journey to accompany the creations of Nikula.
creator: justine

title: Screening: The Summer Book
content:
Screening: The Summer Book (2025),
In the presence of director Charlie McDowell
Thursday, 18 June 2026 – 7pm
Institut finlandais

Based on Tove Jansson’s beloved novel for adults, published in 1972, the film tells the magical and life-affirming story of a girl named Sophia spending the summer with her grandmother on a small island in the Gulf of Finland. As the waves lap against the rocks, the sun shines and the trees grow, the tender, deep bond between them grows stronger with each adventure they share. On screen, the Finnish summer unfolds in all its authenticity and beauty.

The film stars Glenn Close, eight-time Academy Award nominee, and 10-year-old Finnish actress Emily Matthews, making her film debut alongside Anders Danielsen Lie, Pekka Strang, Sophia Heikkilä and Ingvar Sigurdsson.

The film is directed by Charlie McDowell and the screenplay is written by Robert Jones. The Summer Book was filmed in Finland, including along the coast of the Gulf of Finland, in the archipelagos of Kotka and Porvoo.

In English with French subtitles.

title: CHARGE
content:
Charge is a site-specific dance performance that investigates the act of charging itself – and dares the human body to become a battery.

The piece draws its energy from an eclectic constellation of inspirations: superheroes and their mythologies, electro-acoustic and techno music (including the iconic Technotronic hit Pump Up the Jam), the euphoria and exhaustion of the dancing body, the intoxicating speed of Formula 1, the hypnotic loops of video games, and the trance-like power of repetition. At its core, Charge interrogates the unsustainable logic of Western energy production — and searches, with playfulness and urgency, for ways to become its own bionic light source, its own fleshy, self-renewing battery.

Selected from 324 projects submitted across 47 countries, Charge is among 20 finalists performing at Danse Élargie 2026 – one of the world’s most prestigious open-discipline dance competitions.

title: Screening: Tove
content:
Following on from the Visions Nordiques festival in spring 2025, Nordic cinema is returning to Paris in 2026, once a month on a Tuesday at the Grand Action cinema (5 rue des écoles, Paris 5). The month of May will be dedicated to Finnish cinema with the film Tove (2020), directed by Zaida Bergroth.

Awarded Best Film at the Jussi Awards in 2021, Tove offers a novel and romantic take on Tove Jansson, the complex artist behind one of the most iconic creations in children’s literature: the Moomins. A painter and novelist as well, Jansson created a rich and profound artistic world that continues to resonate with new generations in Finland and around the world.

The screening will be followed by a discussion with Zaida Bergroth, filmmaker, and Tuula Yrjö-Koskinen, director of Institut finlandais.

title: Kollektivet
content:
Kollektivet – Picture Book Illustration from Finland
Exhibition from 23 May to 31 July 2026
Inauguration on Friday, 22 May 2026 from 6pm to 8pm

From 23 May to 31 July 2026 at Institut finlandais, Kollektivet features art by a selection of the best Finnish artists and picture book illustrators: Linda Bondestam, Jenni Erkintalo, Lena Frölander-Ulf, Edith Hammar, Maija Hurme, Erika Kallasmaa, Jenny Lucander, Laura Merz, Sanna Pelliccioni and Maria Sann. Together they invite us into a playful, thought-provoking and inclusive world of picture book art that does not shy away from difficult subjects or hope. Picture books are works of art in themselves. In this exhibition, the illustrators’ selected works are brought together under one roof, devoting each artist an own space, while providing an insight into the process from sketch to print-ready material.

title: Jazz at Café Maa n°4 : Aki Rissanen and Dominique Pifarély
content:
On the occasion of UNESCO’s International Jazz Day, the Finnish Institute presents an exceptional concert bringing together two major figures of the European jazz scene: Finnish pianist Aki Rissanen and French violinist Dominique Pifarély.

Echoing a first duo performance in Finland in 2015, the two protagonists—outstanding instrumentalists, composers, and improvisers—reunite at Café Maa for their first appearance in France. Following a solo introduction exploring the sculptural world of the Omniwerk, a one-of-a-kind instrument, Aki Rissanen will be joined by Dominique Pifarély and his intuitive, poetic style. They will continue their dialogue as a violin–piano duo, performing on Institut finlandais’ magnificent Steinway. This fourth edition of Jazz at Café Maa promises to be a unique and deeply human musical performance.

title: Screening series
content:
Screening series
26.3-9.4.2026

With a new season and a new exhibition, Institut finlandais’ big screen is coming to life once again! In this series, we present three contemporary Finnish films from the 2010s, where human relationships are in focus. 

Cross-generational connections arise, paths bend in unexpected directions. Echoing Tommi Toija’s exhibition, the films remind us that when everything seems to be in ruins, the fragments can still come together to build the foundation for something new.

On screening days, our gallery and Café Maa will remain open until the film starts at 7pm. Buy your tickets from our online shop, and enjoy a 5€ discount if you book the full series.

title: Masterclass : Tuija Hakkila
content:
Institut finlandais will host a public piano masterclass led by Finnish pianist Tuija Hakkila on 20 April 2026. The event will take place in two sessions, from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm and 2:00 pm to 5:00 pm, at Institut finlandais, 60 rue des Écoles, 75005 Paris.

The masterclass is intended for advanced young pianists wishing to practice their instrumental work with an internationally recognized artist. Participants are free to choose their repertoire, and each will receive an individual 60-minute lesson.

The sessions are open to auditors. Audience members are invited to reserve one or two time slots, either 10:00 am–1:00 pm or 2:00 pm–5:00 pm, in order to attend the pedagogical work of the pianist. Audience members may enter and leave freely during the reserved time slot.
